name: OpenAI

auth.keyHelp: Create a new secret key; a project key limited to the Models and read endpoints is enough for a connection test (key permission options were not read).

read.label: List models the key can use

write.label: Ask a model something (billed per token)

tested: mock; real service refused a fake key
notes: Base URL https://api.openai.com/v1 and the Authorization: Bearer header come from the API reference overview and the models.list page. platform.openai.com/docs/* pages returned 403 or 301 to developers.openai.com, so developers.openai.com is the source. TEST: GET /models only lists models, changes nothing and is not described as billed; the page does not say it is free, so 'no spend' is the expectation, not a quoted guarantee. It does not name the account, so who is null. KEY PAGE: the overview page names https://platform.openai.com/settings/organization/api-keys for standard keys and .../admin-keys for Administration keys; the quickstart only says 'Create an API Key' in the dashboard. Keys can be project or user keys; multi-organization or legacy user keys should also send the OpenAI-Organization and OpenAI-Project headers (optional, not set here because they are the person's own IDs; IDs live at https://platform.openai.com/settings/organization/general). The overview says the bearer token can also be a short-lived workload identity federation token. Key permission levels (read-only / restricted) were NOT read, so keyHelp does not promise a read-only key. responses.create: the page excerpt was truncated and did not mark a required body field, so only input is listed; model is certainly needed in practice but was not confirmed on the part read. The quickstart example endpoints are /responses and /files. Billing for POST /responses was not stated on the page read. MCP: OpenAI hosts a public, read-only Docs MCP server at https://developers.openai.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP, no auth in the setup examples) covering developers.openai.com, platform.openai.com and learn.chatgpt.com; it is documentation only and does not call the API for the user. The separate 'MCP tool' in the Responses API is a client-side way to point the API at someone else's server and is not an OpenAI-run MCP server.
